lines.text: There's always one decision you shouldn't be making alone.
So build the room. Three to six advisers, each one arguing from their own public record.
Hand them the real numbers. The thing you've been avoiding.
They form their positions in private. Separate agents. No groupthink.
Then the room opens... and they go at each other.
Here's the part nobody else is doing. Your own agent takes a seat.
Eight site tools, live on the page. No integration. Nothing to scrape.
It brings what the board can't know. Your numbers. Your history.
When you've heard enough, you end it. One memo, with the disagreement left in.
The best board meeting you've ever had.
